name: Prometheus
tagline: monitoring, as the Prometheus Operator installs it
description: The Prometheus Operator turns monitoring into Kubernetes objects: a Prometheus is a running server, and the ServiceMonitors, PodMonitors and ScrapeConfigs around it are what it has been told to scrape. This plugin also draws the graphs on pods, nodes, namespaces and the cluster dashboard — those queries assume the metric and label names the kube-prometheus-stack sets up (cAdvisor with a node label, kube-state-metrics, node-exporter). CPU throttling is read from cAdvisor's CFS counters and works on any cluster; pressure (PSI) needs node-exporter on a kernel with PSI for the node charts, and a cgroup v2 kubelet exporting cAdvisor's container_pressure metrics for the pod and namespace ones. If your Prometheus is set up differently, copy this plugin into your own plugins folder under the same id and change the queries.

charts.label: Scrape targets by job
charts.description: How many targets each job is scraping. A job that drops to nothing has lost its endpoints.

charts.label: Scrape targets up by job
charts.description: How many of each job's targets answered their last scrape. Read against the count by job, it is each job's health.

charts.label: Active alerts
charts.description: Every alert that is pending or firing, one series per alert, state, severity and namespace. The overview draws it as the alert timeline and reads what is firing now from its last samples.

charts.label: Targets down
charts.description: Targets Prometheus tried and could not scrape. Anything above zero is a metric you are not getting.

charts.label: Samples ingested
charts.description: Samples appended to the head block per second, across every Prometheus. The pulse of the monitoring itself.

charts.label: Series in memory
charts.description: Active time series in the head block. Memory follows this line; a sudden climb is usually a label with too many values.

charts.label: Firing alerts
charts.description: Alerts in the firing state, by name. Watchdog is meant to be there: it proves the alerting path is alive.

charts.label: TSDB on disk
charts.description: How much disk the Prometheus servers' own blocks take. This grows with the series count and the retention, and is the number to check before a Prometheus fills the volume it is running on.

charts.label: Prometheus volumes full
charts.description: How full the volumes holding Prometheus data are. A Prometheus whose disk fills stops ingesting, which takes every other chart in this app with it — so this is the one to watch.

charts.label: CPU
charts.description: Cores used per container, averaged over five minutes.

charts.label: CPU requested vs used
charts.description: This pod's own request and limit against what it burns. Needs kube-state-metrics. The clearest place to see a request that was guessed rather than measured.

charts.label: CPU throttling
charts.description: Share of CFS periods in which each container was stopped early. A container throttled while using less CPU than it asks for has a limit set below what it actually needs — the clearest reading in the app that a limit, not the cluster, is the thing slowing it down.

charts.label: CPU delay
charts.description: Seconds of throttling per second, per container: how much time it was actually held back, rather than how often. Latency the process itself sees as the CPU simply going away.

charts.label: Pressure (PSI)
charts.description: This pod's worst cgroup, on each of the three pressures. Pressure stall information: the share of time some task was waiting on a resource, and — stalled — the share where every task was. Waiting rising under load is ordinary; stalled is work standing still. Needs a cgroup v2 node whose kubelet exports cAdvisor's container_pressure metrics; older clusters draw nothing here and the throttling charts above are the ones to read.
charts.query: label_replace(max(rate(container_pressure_cpu_waiting_seconds_total{namespace="$namespace",pod="$name"}[5m])), "pressure", "cpu waiting", "", "") or label_replace(max(rate(container_pressure_memory_waiting_seconds_total{namespace="$namespace",pod="$name"}[5m])), "pressure", "memory waiting", "", "") or label_replace(max(rate(container_pressure_memory_stalled_seconds_total{namespace="$namespace",pod="$name"}[5m])), "pressure", "memory stalled", "", "") or label_replace(max(rate(container_pressure_io_waiting_seconds_total{namespace="$namespace",pod="$name"}[5m])), "pressure", "io waiting", "", "") or label_replace(max(rate(container_pressure_io_stalled_seconds_total{namespace="$namespace",pod="$name"}[5m])), "pressure", "io stalled", "", "")

charts.label: Memory
charts.description: Working set per container — what the kernel would have to reclaim, which is what the OOM killer looks at.

charts.label: Memory requested vs used
charts.description: This pod's request and limit against its working set. Needs kube-state-metrics. The working set touching the limit line is what the OOM killer acts on.

charts.label: Network in
charts.description: Bytes received across all of the pod's interfaces.

charts.label: Disk written
charts.description: Ephemeral storage each container is holding: its writable layer, its emptyDirs and its logs. This is what an ephemeral-storage limit bounds, and a container crossing one is evicted rather than throttled.

charts.label: Volumes
charts.description: How much is written in each persistent volume mounted here, as the kubelet on this pod's node reports it. Empty for a pod with no PVCs.

charts.label: Disk read and written
charts.description: Bytes this pod's containers read from and wrote to disk. Read from cAdvisor, so it covers the container filesystem and the volumes mounted into it together.

charts.label: CPU
charts.description: Cores used by everything scheduled on this node.

charts.label: CPU requested vs used
charts.description: What this node has been asked to hold against what it is actually doing. Needs kube-state-metrics.

charts.label: CPU throttling
charts.description: Share of CFS periods in which a container placed here was throttled. High while the node's own CPU line is far from full is limits set too low, not a node too small.

charts.label: CPU delay
charts.description: Seconds of throttling per second across everything on this node — the time its containers spent stopped, waiting for the next CFS period.

charts.label: Pressure (PSI)
charts.description: Pressure stall information: the share of time some task was waiting on a resource, and — stalled — the share where every task was. Waiting rising under load is ordinary; stalled is work standing still. Needs node-exporter on a kernel with PSI. It reports against its own scrape address rather than a node name, so the node is matched on the hostname it reports in node_uname_info — a cluster whose node names are not its hostnames draws nothing here.
charts.query: label_replace(sum(rate(node_pressure_cpu_waiting_seconds_total[5m]) * on (instance) group_left () node_uname_info{nodename=~"$node(\\..*)?"}), "pressure", "cpu waiting", "", "") or label_replace(sum(rate(node_pressure_memory_waiting_seconds_total[5m]) * on (instance) group_left () node_uname_info{nodename=~"$node(\\..*)?"}), "pressure", "memory waiting", "", "") or label_replace(sum(rate(node_pressure_memory_stalled_seconds_total[5m]) * on (instance) group_left () node_uname_info{nodename=~"$node(\\..*)?"}), "pressure", "memory stalled", "", "") or label_replace(sum(rate(node_pressure_io_waiting_seconds_total[5m]) * on (instance) group_left () node_uname_info{nodename=~"$node(\\..*)?"}), "pressure", "io waiting", "", "") or label_replace(sum(rate(node_pressure_io_stalled_seconds_total[5m]) * on (instance) group_left () node_uname_info{nodename=~"$node(\\..*)?"}), "pressure", "io stalled", "", "")

charts.label: Memory
charts.description: Working set of everything scheduled on this node.

charts.label: Memory requested vs used
charts.description: Requested, limits and working set for everything placed on this node. Needs kube-state-metrics.

charts.label: Pods
charts.description: How many pods are placed here. Needs kube-state-metrics.

charts.label: Disk
charts.description: This node's filesystems: how big they are, and how much is written. Needs node-exporter, matched on the hostname it reports in node_uname_info — a cluster whose node names are not its hostnames draws nothing here.

charts.label: Filesystems full
charts.description: How full each of this node's filesystems is. The root filesystem is the one that matters most: when it fills, the kubelet evicts pods to get it back. Needs node-exporter.
charts.query: 1 - (sum by (mountpoint) (node_filesystem_avail_bytes{fstype!~"tmpfs|ramfs|squashfs|overlay|autofs|devtmpfs|iso9660"} * on (instance) group_left () node_uname_info{nodename=~"$node(\\..*)?"}) / sum by (mountpoint) (node_filesystem_size_bytes{fstype!~"tmpfs|ramfs|squashfs|overlay|autofs|devtmpfs|iso9660"} * on (instance) group_left () node_uname_info{nodename=~"$node(\\..*)?"}))

charts.label: Disk throughput
charts.description: Bytes read from and written to this node's disks. A node whose io pressure is climbing while these lines are flat is waiting on something other than its own disk. Needs node-exporter.

charts.label: Container disk written
charts.description: Ephemeral storage held by the containers placed here — writable layers, emptyDirs and logs. The half of this node's disk that Kubernetes itself put there.

charts.label: Cluster CPU
charts.description: Cores used across every workload in the cluster.

charts.label: CPU requested vs used
charts.description: What the scheduler has booked, what those pods may grow into, and what they are really burning. Needs kube-state-metrics. Requested far above used is a cluster paying for room nobody uses; used near limits is a cluster about to throttle.

charts.label: CPU throttling
charts.description: Share of CFS periods in which a container was stopped early because it had spent its slice, across the cluster. Only containers with a CPU limit are ever throttled, so a flat zero means nothing is capped — not that nothing is busy.

charts.label: Most throttled pods
charts.description: The five pods losing the most time to CPU throttling, as seconds of delay per second. A pod at one second per second is spending all of its time waiting for its next slice.

charts.label: Worst node pressure (PSI)
charts.description: The busiest node in the cluster, on each of the three pressures. Pressure stall information: the share of time some task was waiting on a resource, and — stalled — the share where every task was. Waiting rising under load is ordinary; stalled is work standing still. Needs node-exporter on a kernel with PSI (cgroup v2).
charts.query: label_replace(max(rate(node_pressure_cpu_waiting_seconds_total[5m])), "pressure", "cpu waiting", "", "") or label_replace(max(rate(node_pressure_memory_waiting_seconds_total[5m])), "pressure", "memory waiting", "", "") or label_replace(max(rate(node_pressure_memory_stalled_seconds_total[5m])), "pressure", "memory stalled", "", "") or label_replace(max(rate(node_pressure_io_waiting_seconds_total[5m])), "pressure", "io waiting", "", "") or label_replace(max(rate(node_pressure_io_stalled_seconds_total[5m])), "pressure", "io stalled", "", "")

charts.label: Cluster memory
charts.description: Working set across every workload in the cluster.

charts.label: Memory requested vs used
charts.description: Requested, limits and working set across the cluster. Needs kube-state-metrics. Memory limits are the ones that kill: used approaching limits is an OOM waiting to happen.

charts.label: Pods by phase
charts.description: Needs kube-state-metrics. A rising Pending line is the cluster running out of somewhere to put things.

charts.label: API server requests
charts.description: Requests per second by response code, as the API server itself reports them.

charts.label: Node disk
charts.description: The disks under the cluster: how much the nodes have in total, and how much of it is written. This is the one storage every cluster has — persistent volumes need a StorageClass and a provisioner, node disk needs neither. Needs node-exporter.

charts.label: Fullest node filesystems
charts.description: The five filesystems closest to full, anywhere in the cluster. A node whose disk fills stops being able to pull images or write logs, and the kubelet starts evicting pods to get it back. Needs node-exporter.

charts.label: Container disk written
charts.description: Ephemeral storage the containers themselves are holding — writable layers, emptyDirs and logs — across the cluster. This is what an ephemeral-storage limit bounds and what fills a node nobody thought was storing anything.

charts.label: Fullest volumes
charts.description: The five persistent volume claims closest to full. Read from the kubelet's volume stats, so it covers every mounted PVC whatever provisioned it — and covers nothing at all if the cluster has no PVCs.

charts.label: Disk throughput
charts.description: Bytes read from and written to the cluster's disks. Requests and limits say what was promised; this says what the hardware is actually doing, and it is the line that explains io pressure. Needs node-exporter.

charts.label: Busiest disks
charts.description: The five devices spending the largest share of their time serving io. A disk near 100% is saturated whatever its throughput reads, and everything waiting on it is slow. Needs node-exporter.

charts.label: CPU
charts.description: Cores used by the eight busiest pods in this namespace. Eight rather than all of them: a namespace of two hundred pods is a chart nobody can read.

charts.label: CPU throttling
charts.description: Share of CFS periods in which a container in this namespace was throttled. Only containers with a CPU limit are ever throttled, so a flat zero means nothing here is capped.

charts.label: Most throttled pods
charts.description: The five pods here losing the most time to CPU throttling, as seconds of delay per second.

charts.label: Pressure (PSI)
charts.description: The worst-off pod in this namespace, on each of the three pressures. Pressure stall information: the share of time some task was waiting on a resource, and — stalled — the share where every task was. Waiting rising under load is ordinary; stalled is work standing still. Needs a cgroup v2 node whose kubelet exports cAdvisor's container_pressure metrics.
charts.query: label_replace(max(rate(container_pressure_cpu_waiting_seconds_total{namespace="$name"}[5m])), "pressure", "cpu waiting", "", "") or label_replace(max(rate(container_pressure_memory_waiting_seconds_total{namespace="$name"}[5m])), "pressure", "memory waiting", "", "") or label_replace(max(rate(container_pressure_memory_stalled_seconds_total{namespace="$name"}[5m])), "pressure", "memory stalled", "", "") or label_replace(max(rate(container_pressure_io_waiting_seconds_total{namespace="$name"}[5m])), "pressure", "io waiting", "", "") or label_replace(max(rate(container_pressure_io_stalled_seconds_total{namespace="$name"}[5m])), "pressure", "io stalled", "", "")

charts.label: Memory
charts.description: Working set of the eight largest pods in this namespace — what the kernel would have to reclaim, which is what the OOM killer looks at.

charts.label: Disk written
charts.description: The eight pods here holding the most ephemeral storage — writable layers, emptyDirs and logs.

charts.label: Volumes
charts.description: How much is written in each persistent volume claimed in this namespace. Empty for a namespace with no PVCs.

charts.label: Disk written
charts.description: The five pods here writing the most to disk. A pod writing steadily into an emptyDir is the usual way a node's disk fills without anybody noticing.

charts.label: Used
charts.description: What is written in this volume against how big it is, as the kubelet mounting it reports. A claim that is bound but not mounted by a running pod has no reading at all: these come from the kubelet, not from the claim.

charts.label: Full
charts.description: How full the volume is. Where the line is heading matters more than where it is: a volume at 60% and climbing steadily has a date on it, and expanding a PVC is not something to do in a hurry.

charts.label: Inodes used
charts.description: The share of the volume's inodes in use. A filesystem can run out of these while it still has bytes free — the usual cause is a great many small files — and it fails writes exactly as if it were full, which is why it is worth its own line.

charts.label: Replicas
charts.description: Desired is what the spec asks for, ready is how many are passing their probes, available how many have stayed ready long enough to count, and updated how many are on the current template. During a rollout updated climbs to desired; a gap that stays open is a rollout that is stuck. Needs kube-state-metrics.

charts.label: CPU
charts.description: Cores used by each of this Deployment's pods, averaged over five minutes. Gathered from the names of the pods this Deployment makes (<name>-[a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+), because cAdvisor labels a sample with its pod and not with what created it. That shape is Kubernetes' own and holds in practice; a pod renamed out from under it would be missed.

charts.label: Memory
charts.description: Working set of each of this Deployment's pods — what the kernel would have to reclaim, which is what the OOM killer looks at. Gathered from the names of the pods this Deployment makes (<name>-[a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+), because cAdvisor labels a sample with its pod and not with what created it. That shape is Kubernetes' own and holds in practice; a pod renamed out from under it would be missed.

charts.label: Restarts
charts.description: Restarts per pod over the window. A line that steps up repeatedly is a crash loop; one that steps once is a pod that was moved. Gathered from the names of the pods this Deployment makes (<name>-[a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+), because cAdvisor labels a sample with its pod and not with what created it. That shape is Kubernetes' own and holds in practice; a pod renamed out from under it would be missed.

charts.label: Replicas
charts.description: Desired is what the ReplicaSet asks for, replicas how many exist, and ready how many are passing their probes. A ReplicaSet held at zero is an old revision of its Deployment, kept so a rollback has somewhere to go. Needs kube-state-metrics.

charts.label: CPU
charts.description: Cores used by each of this ReplicaSet's pods, averaged over five minutes. Gathered from the names of the pods this ReplicaSet makes (<name>-[a-z0-9]+), because cAdvisor labels a sample with its pod and not with what created it. That shape is Kubernetes' own and holds in practice; a pod renamed out from under it would be missed.

charts.label: Memory
charts.description: Working set of each of this ReplicaSet's pods — what the kernel would have to reclaim, which is what the OOM killer looks at. Gathered from the names of the pods this ReplicaSet makes (<name>-[a-z0-9]+), because cAdvisor labels a sample with its pod and not with what created it. That shape is Kubernetes' own and holds in practice; a pod renamed out from under it would be missed.

That shape is Kubernetes' own and holds in practice; a pod renamed out from under it would be missed.

charts.label: Replicas
charts.description: Desired is how many nodes should be running it, ready how many are, available how many have stayed ready long enough to count, and updated how many are on the current template. Desired climbing on its own is nodes joining the cluster. Needs kube-state-metrics.

charts.label: CPU
charts.description: Cores used by each of this DaemonSet's pods, averaged over five minutes. Gathered from the names of the pods this DaemonSet makes (<name>-[a-z0-9]+), because cAdvisor labels a sample with its pod and not with what created it. That shape is Kubernetes' own and holds in practice; a pod renamed out from under it would be missed.

charts.label: Memory
charts.description: Working set of each of this DaemonSet's pods — what the kernel would have to reclaim, which is what the OOM killer looks at. Gathered from the names of the pods this DaemonSet makes (<name>-[a-z0-9]+), because cAdvisor labels a sample with its pod and not with what created it. charts.label: Replicas
charts.description: Desired is what the spec asks for, ready how many are passing their probes, current how many are on the revision the controller is serving, and updated how many are on the newest one. A StatefulSet rolls one pod at a time, so updated climbs in single steps. Needs kube-state-metrics.

charts.label: CPU
charts.description: Cores used by each of this StatefulSet's pods, averaged over five minutes. Gathered from the names of the pods this StatefulSet makes (<name>-[0-9]+), because cAdvisor labels a sample with its pod and not with what created it. That shape is Kubernetes' own and holds in practice; a pod renamed out from under it would be missed.
